title: analogWrite(9, 64): the timer counts 0…255. How many ticks is the pin HIGH, and what is the duty?
explain: The timer counter runs 0…255 by itself. The pin is HIGH while counter < OCR, so 64 of 256 ticks: 25% duty. The CPU does nothing after analogWrite(). Average voltage = 5 V × 0.25 = 1.25 V.

title: Pot on A0, LED on PWM pin. You use analogWrite(9, value >> 2). What does this print?
explain: x >> 2 is x / 4, and the 2 low bits are dropped. 1020 to 1023 all give 255. You turn a 10-bit ADC value (0…1023) into the 8-bit PWM range (0…255) and lose 2 bits of detail.

title: Where is the output? GND ── 2k ──●── 6k ── 8V. What is the voltage at ●?
explain: Do not trust the drawing. Walk from the output: the part towards GND is R_low (2k), the part towards the supply is R_up (6k). Vout = 8 × 2 / (6 + 2) = 2 V. The small resistor next to GND gives the small voltage.

title: 10 V, 10k on top, 10k at the bottom: 5 V. Now you connect another 10k from the output to GND. New voltage?
explain: The new 10k is in parallel with the bottom 10k, so the bottom becomes 5k. Vout = 10 × 5 / (10 + 5) = 3.33 V. A load changes a voltage divider. Keep the load much bigger than R_low, or buffer the output.

title: Falling edge = last was HIGH and now LOW. The pin samples are below. How many presses are counted?
explain: An edge is a change, not a level. HIGH to LOW happens at index 2 and at index 6: two presses. Checking only s[i] == 0 would count 4. Real buttons bounce, so you also need a debounce of about 50 ms.

title: Next lesson, the servo: 50 Hz signal, 1.5 ms HIGH pulse for the centre position. What duty cycle is that?
explain: 50 Hz gives a 20 ms period. 1.5 / 20 = 7.5% duty. A servo reads the pulse width (about 1 to 2 ms), not the average voltage. That is why analogWrite(127) is wrong for a servo: use the Servo library.

title: Serial prints nothing after some minutes. Tap the bug.
explain: millis() on Uno can jump by 2 ms (the timer ticks every 1.024 ms). If now - previous goes 199 → 201, == 200 is never true again and the difference only grows. With time, use >=, never ==.

title: Button input jumps randomly, LED toggles alone. Tap the bug.
explain: setup() calls pressed() instead of begin(), so pinMode(INPUT_PULLUP) never runs. The pin floats and reads random values. When something is random and unstable, first suspect a floating pin: not connected or not initialised.

title: Multimeter: how V, A and R really work
bullets: V: huge resistance inside (about 10 MΩ). Put it in parallel. It does not change the circuit.
A: tiny shunt resistor inside (about 0.1 Ω), like a wire. Put it in series: break the circuit and insert it. In parallel it is a short circuit.
R: the meter sends its own small current and measures the voltage. Use it only with power off and the part alone.
Wrong mode = wrong or zero reading: A across a resistor pulls the node to GND.

title: You skip the .bss clear in your Reset_Handler. What does static int count; hold at main()?
explain: The C standard says static variables start at 0. But on a microcontroller your startup code makes that true: it zeroes .bss. RAM holds random bits after power-up. .data needs a copy from flash, .bss needs a clear.
